accepted.question_text: In the adversarial contextual bandit setting with context space X, finite action space A = {1, ..., K}, horizon T, and a nested sequence of finite policy classes Π1 ⊂ Π2 ⊂ ⋯ ⊂ ΠM, does there exist an algorithm that simultaneously guarantees, for every m ∈ [M], expected regret to class Πm of order O(√(KT(log |Πm| + log m)))? Here regret to Πm means max over π ∈ Πm of E[Σ_t ℓt(at) − Σ_t ℓt(π(xt))].

evidence.quote: Focusing on contextual bandits, a simple reinforcement learning setting, we ask: Can model selection guarantees be achieved in contextual bandit learning, where a learner must balance exploration and exploitation to make decisions online?
Open Problem 1a Design a contextual bandit algorithm that for any sequence Π1 ⊂ Π2 ⊂ ⋯ΠM ensures max π∈Πm E[ T ∑ t=1 ℓt(at) − T ∑ t=1 ℓt(π(xt))] ≤ O( √KT(log∣Πm∣ + log m)), for all m ∈ [M].

accepted.question_text: In the same adversarial contextual bandit setting with nested finite policy classes Π1 ⊂ Π2 ⊂ ⋯ ⊂ ΠM, can one design a model-selection algorithm that for every m ∈ [M] either (1) achieves regret Reg(Πm) ≤ O(poly(K, M, log log |Π|) · √(T log |Πm|)), or (2) achieves regret Reg(Πm) ≤ O(poly(K, M, log log |Π|) · T^α log^(1−α) |Πm|) for some α ∈ [1/2, 1)? Alternatively, can one prove that no algorithm can achieve the second type of guarantee for any α ∈ [1/2, 1)?

evidence.quote: Open Problem 1b Design a contextual bandit algorithm that for any sequence Π1 ⊂ Π2 ⊂ ⋯ΠM ensures either: 1. Reg(Πm) ≤ O(poly(K,M, log log∣Π∣) ⋅ √T log∣Πm∣) for all m ∈ [M]. 2. Reg(Πm) ≤ O(poly(K,M, log log∣Π∣) ⋅ T α log1−α ∣Πm∣) for all m ∈ [M], where α ∈ [1/2, 1). Alternatively, prove that no algorithm can achieve item 2 above for any value α ∈ [1/2, 1).

accepted.question_text: In stochastic realizable contextual bandits, suppose (xt, ℓt) are drawn i.i.d. from a fixed distribution D, each policy class Πm is induced by a regression class Fm ⊂ (X × A → [0, 1]) via πf(x) = argmin_a f(x, a), and there exist m⋆ and f⋆ ∈ Fm⋆ such that E[ℓ(a) | x] = f⋆(x, a) for all contexts x and actions a. Is there, for some α ∈ [1/2, 1), an algorithm whose expected regret to the optimal policy πf⋆ is O(poly(K, M, log log |F|) · T^α log^(1−α) |Fm⋆|)? Alternatively, can one prove that no algorithm can achieve this guarantee for any α ∈ [1/2, 1)?

evidence.quote: Open Problem 2 For some value α ∈ [1/2, 1), design an algorithm for contextual bandits that for any sequence F1 ⊂ F2 ⊂ ⋯FM = F, whenever data is stochastic and realizable, ensures E[ T ∑ t=1 ℓt(at) − T ∑ t=1 ℓt(πf⋆ (xt))] ≤ O(poly(K,M, log log∣F∣) ⋅ T α log1−α ∣Fm⋆ ∣). Alternatively, prove that no algorithm can achieve this guarantee for any value of α ∈ [1/2, 1).

accepted.question_text: In full-information online learning, does there exist an algorithm such that for every ε > 0 it simultaneously achieves regret at most O(√(Σ_t Var_{π∼Pt}(ℓt(π(xt))) · log(1/ε))) against the top ε-quantile of policies, where Pt is the algorithm's distribution over policies at round t?

evidence.quote: An unresolved COLT 2016 open problem of Freund (2016) asks whether there exists an algorithm for this setting with regret at most O( √ ∑ T t=1 Varπ∼Pt (ℓt(π(xt))) ⋅ log(1/ε)) against the top ε-quantile of policies for all ε > 0 simultaneously.
